newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Milling wheat drops, maize firms on Hungary's BCE.
newsitem.headline: Milling wheat drops, maize firms on Hungary's BCE.

text.p: Milling wheat futures on the Budapest Commodity Exchange continued to drop on Friday, while maize futures closed higher due to what traders said was a technical correction following recent falls.
August to December milling wheat prices were allowed to move freely on Friday as they had fallen by the 400-forint limit for five consecutive days.
But only the September and August maturities fell by more than 400 forints, which indicated that the decline of milling wheat prices was likely to slow down, traders said.
"The fall of milling wheat seems to continue, but not nearly with the same impetus as so far," said Tamas Kobulniczky of Swap Ugynoki Kft.
May milling wheat futures closed at 24,800 forints, down by only 50 forints, while the July maturity, which is in freefall, dropped 1,000 forints in brisk trading, to close at 19,850.
Maize futures that traded on Friday finished steady to higher.

"Earlier sellers are now liquidating their positions and trying to take profits," Kobulniczky said, adding that the 500,000 to one-million tonne surplus of maize in the country was likely to trigger further falls in maize futures.
March maize closed at 17,400 forints, up 190, while July firmed 250 to end at 16,950 forints.
Lot size is 20,000 kg for all contracts.
